recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Shared types & foundation
recommended_phases.rationale: All modules depend on shared-types. Establish the enums (LeaveType, LeaveStatus, AuditAction, EmploymentStatus) and base repository pattern first. No downstream modules can compile without these.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Employee & LeavePolicy modules
recommended_phases.rationale: These are leaf modules with no inter-module dependencies beyond shared-types. Employee provides identity/manager lookups; LeavePolicy provides entitlement rules. Both are prerequisites for leave-request and leave-balance.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — Audit & Notification modules
recommended_phases.rationale: Cross-cutting infrastructure modules. Audit records all state changes (GP-002); Notification sends alerts on status transitions. Both depend only on shared-types and are consumed by leave-request.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — LeaveBalance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on shared-types and leave-policy (for entitlement rules). Must exist before leave-request can deduct/restore balances during approval/rejection workflows.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5 — LeaveRequest module (core orchestration)
recommended_phases.rationale: The orchestrating module. Depends on all other modules: validates against policy, checks balances, resolves employee/manager, writes audit records, sends notifications. Contains the controller and routes — the API surface.

app_notes: Layer boundaries: presentation (routes/controllers in leave-request module), application (service interfaces + implementations in each module), domain (models in each module), infrastructure (repositories in each module, db connection in shared/db). Dependencies flow inward: leave-request (outermost, orchestrates) → leave-balance, leave-policy, employee, audit, notification → shared-types (innermost). No circular dependencies — verified: the dependency graph is a DAG with shared-types at the root, then leaf modules (employee, leave-policy, audit, notification), then leave-balance (depends on leave-policy), then leave-request at the top depending on all others. Every public service method is declared in an interface before implementation. Shared enums (LeaveType, LeaveStatus, AuditAction, EmploymentStatus) placed in src/shared/types/ per the shared-value-type rule since they are pure data shapes used by multiple modules.

open_questions.question: When should leave balance be deducted — at approval time or on the leave start date?
open_questions.impact: Affects deductBalance, restoreBalance, and recalculateRemainingDays semantics across leave-balance and leave-request modules. If deducted at approval, a cancelled leave must restore. If deducted at start date, the balance check at approval is a reservation/hold, not a deduction.
candidate_options: Deduct at approval time (simpler; restore on rejection/cancellation)
Reserve at approval, deduct on start date (more accurate for overlapping requests but adds reservation state)
Deduct at approval but recalculate remainingDays as totalEntitlement - usedDays - pendingDays (hybrid)

open_questions.question: Should the system prevent overlapping leave requests for the same employee?
open_questions.impact: Affects validateLeaveRequest in ILeavePolicyService and the createLeaveRequest flow in ILeaveRequestService. Without overlap detection, an employee could be approved for two leaves covering the same dates, making balance tracking unreliable.
candidate_options: Reject overlapping date ranges at submission time
Allow overlaps but warn the manager during approval

auth_contract: Authenticated request shape: request.user = { id: string; role: UserRole }. UserRole enum: 'employee' | 'manager' | 'hr_admin'. Identity obtained via JWT bearer token verified by an auth middleware (verifyJwt) that populates request.user. RBAC enforced by a requireRole(...) route-level guard, never inline. Endpoints: POST /leave-requests (employee), PATCH /leave-requests/:id/submit (employee, own requests only), PATCH /leave-requests/:id/approve (manager, team members only), PATCH /leave-requests/:id/reject (manager, team members only), GET /leave-requests (employee sees own; manager sees team; hr_admin sees all).
error_response_contract: Standard error shape: { error: string; code: string; details?: unknown }. Validation failure → HTTP 400 { error: "Validation failed", code: "VALIDATION_ERROR", details: [...] }. Authentication failure → HTTP 401 { error: "Authentication required", code: "UNAUTHORIZED" }. Authorization failure → HTTP 403 { error: "Insufficient permissions", code: "FORBIDDEN" }. Not found → HTTP 404 { error: "Resource not found", code: "NOT_FOUND" }. Conflict (e.g. insufficient balance, overlapping dates) → HTTP 409 { error: "...", code: "CONFLICT" }.
